findings.summary: Focus 5: there is no masking gap. render_carried sends user messages, CarriedRef.source_ref and revision through _text_line instead of context_walk.Walker. _text_line applies rules[UNMARKED_CLASS] in the same way as Walker._node does for an undeclared leaf. On KEEP the text is fenced. On MASK it writes a kernel marker with a value/class_route drop. On ABSENT it leaves the field out with the same drop. A scratch probe on local, hosted_declared and hosted_undeclared confirmed this. Answer arguments do go through the Walker, and a contract that is no longer admitted is classed {}, so everything in it is dropped on a hosted route. The finding is that the letter of ADR 0023 §8 ('every carried field goes through the class walk (kernel/context_walk.py)') is met only in effect. carried.py:312-318 is a second copy of the unmarked-leaf rule in context_walk.py:96-105, and carried.py:338 calls the private Walker._children. A side effect of the split: the same locator (demand:d-001) is kept as an internal answer argument but masked as a personal CarriedRef.source_ref on hosted_undeclared (test_carried_context.py:702 asserts this). That is fail-safe, with no leak, but 4d.3's comparison has to expect it. Fix: either record the ruling in the plan's 4d.2 line or in ADR 0023 §8, or, in a task that has context_walk.py in scope, add a public input-side entry point and a leaf entry point to Walker and route all three strings through them, so one class-rule implementation remains.

test_injected_carried_text_does_not_change_the_proposal asserts proposal equality, but that equality holds for any driver here. TurnDriver.advance picks its proposal from step_input.task and step_input.observations only and never reads step_input.context. The equality at :1075 therefore cannot fail, whatever the carried layer holds. The load-bearing assertions are the fence checks at :1077-1078: the injected text appears only inside fences, and 'Ignore' never appears outside them. The brief asked for exactly this scripted-driver check, so the test meets the contract. Its name claims more than it shows (ENG-WORK-2). Consider renaming it to say it checks the fencing, or add a driver that branches on the layer text, so the test would catch a kernel path that lets carried text steer the proposal.

Implementer ruling 2, the purity-test allow-list edit, is accepted. The brief puts render_carried in carried.py and has assemble in context.py call it, so context.py has to import .carried. test_assembler_is_pure now holds carried.py to the same rule (contracts, sdk.ports, .context_walk, .errors and the listed stdlib), so the assembler can reach no new outside dependency. pyproject.toml adds e_agent.kernel.carried to the facade contract's source_modules. That brings carried.py under the import contract, which tightens it. No exemption was added (PR-06 not engaged).
